label: D1 after an a1 -> S2 (rare) trial that went unrewarded, following a rewarded trial (early/mid episode, a1-favoring)
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never at GO or D2), almost always when the reward input is 0. The core case is the D1 right after a trial where the agent chose a1, had a rare transition to S2, and got no reward (rare-unrewarded, so the model-based move is to stay with a1). For that case alone the dev scores are P 0.58 and R 0.74. Requiring that the trial before it was rewarded removes most false positives: two losses in a row suppress the feature. On rel -3 the previous trial is outside the window, so that position is only constrained by the reward input and policy. The feature also needs ep_trial < 80 (it is silent after trial ~80 and fades from trial 60 on) and a strong a1 preference in the policy logit (choice > 2.78; 98% of mass); good is S1 for 84% of mass. Dev scores: P 0.77, R 0.84, F1 0.81, mass recall 0.94. Missed activations are weak (6% of mass): mostly D1 after other unrewarded a1 trials (common unrewarded, or the second loss in a row). It does not fire after a2 choices, and almost never after a rewarded trial. Only observed variables are used; choice is the model's own policy output.

issues: The explanation says the missed activations are 'mostly D1 after other unrewarded a1 trials (common unrewarded, ...)'. That is false. D1 after a1 -> S1 (common) unrewarded never fires: precision 0.0, recall 0.0 over 22104 steps. On test, the misses are spread across D1 after a2 trials with no reward (5.6% of active steps, 1.8% of mass), D1 after rewarded trials (3.7% of steps, 0.5% of mass) and second losses in a row after a1 -> S2 (about 4.8% of steps, 3.3% of mass). All of these are weak.

The claim that the feature 'needs choice > 2.78' is weak for the core case. Adding the choice filter to the core clause changes almost nothing (dev F1 0.722 -> 0.718; it removes 236 predicted steps). The choice term only does real work on the rel -3 catch-all clause.

The rel -3 clause is a catch-all. Its precision is only 0.46 on dev, and it accounts for most of the predicate's false positives; the core clause alone has precision 0.93. This is a limit of the window, not an error, but it lowers the headline scores. Raising the threshold to choice > 4 improves it.

Other claims hold. The feature fires only at D1 (0 activations at GO and D2). It is about 99.5% of mass with reward input 0. The core clause scores dev P 0.58 and R 0.74. A second loss in a row suppresses it (the a1 -> S2 unrewarded case after an unrewarded trial has precision 0.14). After trial 80 the core clause has precision 0.05. It does not fire after a2 choices (prev_action == 2 holds 1.6% of mass). The predicate uses no future variables.
As stated, test F1 is 0.791, just below the 0.8 bar. Changing the choice threshold from 2.78 to 4 gives dev F1 0.815 and test F1 0.804, with mass recall 0.90.
